A.claim: Document-writing canonical ops have PERM-COM-free because their sig was cut at the first '|': raster.write, transform.set, key.delete, mask.create, node.reorder, node.align, node.distribute. A plugin with no grant can write pixels and geometry.

Every OP-COM-platform-* family row lists PERM-COM-free, so its sensitive ops carry no enforced permission. These include process.run, os.openUrl/handoff, fonts.install (system), input.monitor, media.capture and history.snapshot.restore. Some ops also have a duplicate record with different perms.

Gate step 9 runs the write-set check only for selection scope. Other records say it runs after every step and at commit. A plugin with a scoped grant (layer, file or document subset) could write outside its ScopeToken.

Three records describe the single gate with different entry points and step orders. CMP-SEC-ext-runtime-gate and this record use authorize(rt,call)->Authorized with policy and admit_path steps. OP-COM-gate-admit uses admit(call,cx)->Admitted with shape and mem but no policy step.

Several ops require app.automation even though that permission covers only edits from automatic events. Affected: events.subscribe (any event), timer.after/every, txn.modal, txn.group, pkg.read/pkg.open and gate::admit. Every panel or executeAsModal port would have to ask for an L1 automation grant.

cmd! refuses intercept and override flags on view, selection, nudge and tool commands. DEC-COM-hooks-generic-intercept says intercept and user-chosen override cover view, selection and nudge commands. Launcher and automation plugins cannot replace tool or selection behaviour.

FigCraft's owner wake breaks the common contract. on_owner calls request_repaint on every push, and drain_owner runs from eframe::App::update (the paint callback). With no owner-queue cap, a flooding plugin forces a repaint per call, and work stops when the window is occluded.

FigCraft's panic scenario and test still depend on guard::run and 'poison the event', but CMP-COM-contain deletes guard::run. contain rolls back to the call's mark and returns -7 with no strike. Which behaviour is tested is undefined, and CMP-COM-contain has no tests of its own.

Hot render-path contracts have budget 'no numeric budget stated': audio.effect/instrument (real-time), raster.filter@2.0, gpu.kernel, video.transition, viewport.overlay, tool@1.0, nn and anim.ease. Check C13 sees a budget string, so only the missing bench is flagged.

The gate returns -9 Excluded {NetworkPath}, and node-compat network modules return -9, but the error table lists only NetworkMidi, NetworkUsb and LocalSocket under -9. Gate C20 fails on any unlisted detail.kind, so the gate and the table cannot both pass.

iOS builds run plugins in-process (wasmi, and QuickJS per DEC-COM-languages-all-day-one). Gate C24 forbids any app from constructing a script runtime in its own process, and no record says how an in-process plugin's OOM, panic or stall is contained.
Plugin-origin print always shows a dialog, and printer and endpoint params are agent-only. Batch and automation tools cannot print silently or choose a printer, and no record gives a cause.

B.claim: Canonical write ops whose sig holds '|' (transform.set, raster.write, node.reorder/align/distribute, mask.create, key.delete, export.render, asset.import) carry PERM-COM-free; sig is cut at the pipe, so perms came from a mis-split column and these writes are ungated.

Platform group rows (process.*, os.*, input.*, media.*, fonts.*, clipboard.*, plugins.*, service.*, bus.*, settings.*) list only PERM-COM-free, but their ops need process.run:<id>, os.open, input.monitor, media.capture, fonts.system, clipboard.read, plugins.control, bus:<topic>.

pkg.read/pkg.open require app.automation though they are free; events.subscribe and txn.modal/txn.group also demand app.automation, and OP-FC-export.render always demands files.any, restrictions with no cause that block read-only panels and buffer exports.

gate::admit runs the write-set check only for selection scope and has no admit_path or policy step, while CON-SEC-gate-authorize@1 orders admit_path and policy and requires the write-set check after every step and at commit; Params("layer") scopes escape the check.

An ordinary live holder is aborted by any user edit, peer apply or another plugin waiting 250 ms, and the SDK retries once; in a busy live session or with two event-driven plugins a long non-modal event livelocks and never commits.
iOS builds run plugins in-process on wasmi (and QuickJS per CAP-COM-sdk-ts-js), so a guest-driven host panic, stack overflow or OOM kills the app, against the no in-process plugin code rule.
Bans interceptable/overridable on view, selection and nudge commands, while DEC-COM-hooks-generic-intercept grants intercept and user-chosen override including view, selection and nudge commands.

Overlay (plugin-contributed) commands are 'refused through the bridge (rule 7) and reached through service.call', but rule 7 is Url and rule 13 sends plugin-contributed commands through plugins.run under plugins.control.

Long commands (edit.contentAwareFill, actions.play, 47 EffectCraft long jobs) are callable only via job.runCommand, a separate job and step, so a modal retouch sequence cannot be one history step and actions.play cannot be a savepointed run.

figma-compat getters read a worker mirror updated only by the plugin's own writes while setters wait in cx.edit, so host-derived fields (auto-layout child x/y, absoluteBoundingBox, text auto-resize size, fillGeometry) stay stale after a set.

Budgets accept slower than incumbent: JS1 allows 2x the Figma iframe time, and S-NODE allows 1 ms p99 per sync fs.statSync from a CEF page, about 100x native Node, so a 10k-file library walk takes 10 s.

node-compat exec with shell syntax runs under a 'shell declaration', but CAP-EC-route-process-run and CON-SEC-sink-set@1 allow only declared, identity-pinned executables with validated argv and never a shell.

A.claim: The 12-renderer cap and discard ladder kill hidden UXP/CEP plugin pages, and those pages hold each plugin's only JS context. A user with more than 12 enabled UXP plugins loses commands and notification listeners, and a 13th visible web panel gets -6 Budget.

Synchronous batchPlay with synchronousExecution goes through __sync, which has a 2 ms p99 budget and a hard 5 s timeout (PageSyncTimeout). Heavy synchronous commands that finish in Photoshop throw here instead.

ui.web.open lists PERM-COM-none, but PERM-COM-ui.web (L1) exists, and CAP-FC-kind-web-window says the op needs ui.web. CAP-COM-surface-t6-palette-semantics calls the op free. The permission and its context rule (no visible pages in automatic contexts) are not enforced at the op.

The ui.window.open, close, setSize and setTitle ops all require ui.window:floating or the elevated grant, but palette windows are free. As written, a plugin cannot open or resize its own free palette or host-opened modal window without a grant.

UXP auxiliary panel browsers must share the opener's agent cluster. In CEF the only way to get that is a renderer popup through OnBeforePopup, and window.open is cancelled in the engine for every page, so ext-web::panel_browser cannot be built as specified.

The only page-to-plugin bridge carries JSON of at most 1 MiB with no transfer list. Figma UIs that post Uint8Array images to main cannot send large bytes, which contradicts the PhotoCraft record and the post op that both move ArrayBuffers as Handle(Bytes).

The record says its caps are 'the only limits', yet other records add caps. PhotoCraft overlays allow 20,000 ops and 2,000 regions against 100,000 and 10,000. Toasts are 3 at 1/s, start cards 200 nodes, media decoders 8, renderers 12.
The plugin overlay is defined three times with different shapes. A plugin cannot target all apps with one overlay call, which breaks the 'behaviour in one place' rule.

Behaviour and painting are duplicated in several places. The craft-libs ui crate ships its own T3 components (CurveEditor, NodeGraph and others) next to ui-editors-core. Setup sheets have an 'egui twin' and two named builders. The FigCraft framework swap adds a second 'framework renderer'.

Owner decision D-D is recorded nine times with different recommendations: DEC-PC gives 'CefDockedCompat or CefDocked', others give CefDocked. The records also disagree on whether policy may lower the web mode. CAP records cite different copies.

Working state for modal and gesture transactions is published at no more than 30 Hz. On 60 and 120 Hz displays, a plugin's drag or warp result therefore updates at half or a quarter of frame rate, while incumbent transform and Liquify previews track at display rate.

Two per-frame hot paths have no time budget. The input pump's budget is 'steps in fixed order', and the when grammar's is 'evaluated each frame'. Neither bounds the UI-thread cost of routing an event or of evaluating every plugin's when-expressions.

Digests with unbounded loops or parameters without a form max get promoted after 120 good frames, then run inline before UI present. A later parameter change can then hold the UI up to the 1 s watchdog. Demotion only happens after a 4x EMA overrun has already been seen.
Says promoted L3 lists run in the plugin submit after the UI and compositor. R40 says promoted digests run inline in the document render, before UI present.

Permits are cores minus the app render threads of every running app, with no floor. With two or three apps open, or on a 4-core machine, the count reaches 0 or goes negative, and every render-class plugin call stalls until its deadline.

GpuSubmit is a fixed 4 ms per inline segment. It is not a Vsync fraction, and nothing caps the total of all inline segments plus Paint in one frame. At 120 or 240 Hz, or with several promoted plugins, the frame budget cannot be met.
native.start, native.call and native.ring are marked PERM-COM-free, but the contract says native.start needs native.restricted or native.full. As recorded, the permission is not enforced.

These host-internal functions carry PERM-COM-gpu.direct, so CPU, L1 and L2 filter planning and every account charge would appear to need a permission that is meant only for L3. OP-COM-account-charge and OP-COM-budget-resolve have the same problem.

Records disagree on who pays for staging, document growth and durable output. One says DocGrowth, surfaces, readbacks and durable data go to the plugin account; others say they are spillable app cache that never touches the plugin account. The answer decides whether upscalers fail with -6.
This record says every backend except WGSL runs in craft-nn-helper. Other records say CPU tract runs in the worker. That changes the crash surface, the seeded-determinism path and nn.infer latency.

The macOS launch path is open with an owner (decide by QoS at USER_INTERACTIVE), while DEC-SEC-launch-path-5ms is already decided by a different rule (S-W1 acceptance plus spawn in 5 ms or less). The two acceptance rules can choose different paths.

These acceptance targets allow plugins to run slower than the incumbent: up to 2x UXP V8 for JS, and up to 1.5x native AVX2 or NEON for Nik or Silver Efex-class filters. The incumbent rows are not matched at the same speed.

In FigCraft, L1-L3 filters, previews and GPU nn.run run on a separate job device, so results reach the canvas device through readback and upload. That breaks zero-copy, the common rule that probation runs on the app device, and the rule that WGSL nn runs on the app device.

The IPC round-trip budget of p50 5 us or less and p99 20 us or less has no power-state qualifier. The S-W1 rows allow p99 up to 100 us on Saver and Critical, where the serving side never spins, so the hot-path budget cannot be met on battery as written.

B.claim: Render permits are capped at cores minus app render threads of all apps, with no floor. With EffectCraft MFR using about cores-1 threads, plugin effects get 0 or 1 permit. Every plugin frame then waits on a worker that cannot run and falls down the ladder.

Plugins may not ship a codec for user-picked files, and host image.decode/encode does not list DDS, KTX2 or BCn. As written, the NVIDIA Texture Tools row (DDS import/export through format.import@1) cannot be built.

The acceptance bars let plugins run slower than incumbents. JS pixel loops may take 2x UXP on the same V8 engine, and the CPU1 Silver Efex-class filter may take 1.5x native AVX2/NEON. Ported UXP and Nik-class plugins would be slower.

Records disagree on who pays for plugin-caused growth. Some charge every allocation made for a plugin (DocGrowth, pinned tiles, durable output) to that plugin. Others charge filter outputs, staging, durable outputs and model pages to spillable app cache, which plugins are never allowed to evict.

Three host-internal functions (tiles::plan, budget::resolve, account::charge) carry PERM-COM-gpu.direct, which covers only L3 GPU programs. If the gate enforces it, every tiled CPU filter needs gpu.direct, which is a restriction with no cause. If not, the perms field is wrong.

job.spawn and job.runCommand require app.automation, a permission for edits from automatic events. A user-started background job (tracking, roto, matte, upscale) edits nothing until it is applied, so this blocks long-running jobs with no cause.

The Saver budget for a dependent read (p50 <=15 us) is tighter than the Ac budget (20 us), yet the serving side never spins on Saver. A parked futex or os_sync wake per call cannot meet a budget that Ac, with both sides spinning, only meets at 20 us.

Records disagree on where CPU tract runs. CAP-COM-nn-backends and DEC-COM-v1-23 put it in the worker. DEC-COM-ai-backends and CMP-COM-craft-nn put everything except WGSL in craft-nn-helper. Determinism, crash attribution and the ONNX parser crash surface depend on which is true.

The 27 traced INC/API rows hang on PROPOSED capabilities that duplicate spec or decided records. Codec, NN, GPU tier and device-loss capabilities each exist twice, so incumbents such as remove-bg, Topaz and Filter Forge never trace to an adjudicated capability.

Dirty out and state pages stay resident until the stroke ends, and the default 256 MiB interactive quota holds 512 pages, about 33 MP for one texture. A 2,000 px stroke across a 100 MP canvas fails with -6 and rolls back.
gpu.timing is already a granted permission, yet timestamps are still quantised to 100 us. Passes of 0.18 ms cannot be profiled, while threads=shared gives nanosecond CPU timing at L1.

Several tests verify records they do not exercise. Tile planner tests verify the sandbox launcher and ext-ipc, a memory test verifies the web backend, and a JS bench verifies iOS hosting. CON-EC-gpu-probation@1 names craft-aehost and file-snapshot test K1.

A.claim: Handoff starts the user's own installed vendor app (Topaz, Luminar Neo, DxO) with network denied, and in an AppContainer on Windows. Online activation, on-demand model downloads and per-user settings then fail. Yet companion and daemon vendor apps keep internet access with a disclosure.

Provenance is keyed by (device, inode, size, mtime, sha256) and recorded only for fs-broker creates. Writes through brokered fds held by restricted helpers or confined processes, and later appends, change the key, so plugin-written .jsx/.atn run with user authority.

Without Landlock (kernel <5.13 or disabled), restricted helpers and confined processes still run, with only a notice. Their file confinement to the data folder plus brokered handles is not enforced, so an L3 grant silently becomes user-wide file access.
The vocabulary rule is one level per name, with broader names covering narrower ones, but derived and op-level rows carry other levels. Setup sheets and risk() therefore disagree with gate::derive.

The host-only trust action that removes taint has three permissions across records: free in EffectCraft, app.session (L1) in PhotoCraft, and 'never plugin-visible (N1)' in PhotoCraft's own text. A plugin with free or app.session access can reach the trust sheet for its scripts.

T6 is refused on browsers without the CSP webrtc directive. Chrome, Edge and Firefox lack it, so every iframe-UI plugin fails on web builds. CAP-COM-t6-web-builds lists only the Navigation API condition, so behaviour is split across records.

Licensing daemons reached over localhost IP (CodeMeter, Sentinel LDK) are refused, but Unix-socket daemons are allowed. The cause is the transport, not the risk, so plugins using those licence runtimes cannot load.

Linux full-mode Landlock refuses new entries directly in $HOME, entries created after launch, and user-writable mounts outside /media, /mnt and /tmp (e.g. /data, /srv). native.full and files.write:any promise everything except persist paths. Kernel floors also disagree: 5.9 vs 5.13.

lpac_com_native_ui defaults to false behind a test gate, so hosted Windows 8bf/AE/OFX UIs that need out-of-proc COM (shell file dialogs, WIC) fail. Holding a capability off until gate C-LPAC passes is a deferral.

The brokered device hot paths have no latency or throughput budget: USB streaming, PTP live view, scanner bands and capture.frames. Each frame takes an extra broker hop, so tethered live view and capture may not match native speed.
Redaction runs on every intercept payload, including input.filter and pen.filter at stylus rates, but its budget has no number. Only overridden nudges have a numeric bound.

Two records describe the same companion-controller capability through different permissions: native.restricted (L3) and devices.companion:<id> (L2). Sheets, levels and tests (TST-COM-cc1 vs TST-COM-cc1-companion) diverge.
Monolith's permission sheet is L0 with no gpu.direct, yet it uses the full L3 command set. Either the gpu.direct gate is not enforced or the flagship cannot run as written.

Tempo's L0 sheet leaves out gpu.direct (needed for its L3 flow pyramids) and app.automation (needed for its job.spawn pre-pass). Isolate's 'export at full model size as a job' also lacks app.automation.

Particular picks light emitters by name and Optical Flares picks light sources by name, which needs comp.layers. Ember's and Halo's sheets stop at read:selection, and validation refuses comp.layers without read:document, so these features cannot be matched.

Ember's 640 MB of particle state cannot fit a GPU checkpoint (256 MiB quota), so each checkpoint costs about 26 ms of readback during RAM preview. A 2 GiB disk cap holds only 3 checkpoints, so seeks and export degrade to near-serial stepping, and no budget covers this.

render.output@1 delivers only ordered colour frames and audio, with no aux channels. Strata/ProEXR 'write every aux channel of a render as EXR layers' therefore has no path. Aux channels are also per-layer (LayerResult.aux), and no comp-level aux composition is defined.

The Lockdown-class mesh solver writes a per-frame mesh into a data param stored as a document blob. However, track.solver@1's host write targets are only track points, Corner Pin or Transform keys, and camera plus nulls, so a returned mesh has nowhere to land.

A hard cap of 8 named aux outputs per effect, also inherited by renderer3d@1, has no stated cause. It blocks Cineware-class multipass, which commonly exports more than 8 passes and object buffers from one render.

On macOS, craft-aehost reaches vendor licensing daemons (maxon, borisfx). Windows LPAC grants no daemon or local-IPC reach, so installed Universe, Sapphire and Continuum cannot license on Windows. That breaks same-milestone parity.

system.callSystem routes to process.run, which allows a 'full' launch path, so a submitter can run deadlinecommand or curl and reach the network. That breaks the no-plugin-network rule. The folder hand-off also has no way to track job status, and Lockdown's CEP Node path has the same hole.

Each Stardust-class graph edit makes a new digest. Atomics-driven generated modules go back on probation for 120 frames, running as tiled submits after the UI present with the walk split. Interactive graph editing can never match the incumbent's inline speed.

The host trait's FxFail has exactly Degrade, Failed and Cancelled, but the guest SDK returns FxError::NoGpu, and no mapping between them is defined. Whether NoGpu falls back to the CPU render, degrades, or fails the frame is undefined.

Interchange is RGBA32F only in a 32-bpc project, yet Deep Glow-class effects declare accepts=["rgba32f"] only. Behaviour in 8- and 16-bpc projects (convert with a copy, or refuse) is unspecified, and it conflicts with 'host picks the cheapest' and output_intermediate_copies=0.

B.claim: The aehost selector map has no row for PF_Cmd_GPU_DEVICE_SETUP/SETDOWN, FRAME_SETUP/SETDOWN, QUERY_DYNAMIC_FLAGS, COMPLETELY_GENERAL, TRANSLATE_PARAMS_TO_PREFS or RESET, and lists no DirectX GPU framework. Hosted GPU and non-smart AE binaries cannot run.
Unbounded-loop L2/L3 modules on probation run on EffectCraft's own device on D3D12 and Vulkan. A hung dispatch causes a driver TDR, which loses the whole app device, so a plugin can stall the app.

Monolith's capabilities need the full L3 command set, but its permission sheet has no gpu.direct, so either the gate is not enforced or the flagship cannot run. Tempo's 'L2/L3 compute' sheet has the same gap.

The EffectCraft L2 tier allows render passes (vertex/fragment, depth, MSAA, instancing), but the security record admits only compute or fragment modules, so 3D Stroke- and Plexus-class L2 render passes have no validated path.

Output expansion is clamped to the comp plus 4096 px, with no stated cause, while AE allows expand buffers up to 30,000 px layers. Glows and flares on scaled-down precomps or collapsed layers get clipped.
Each effect is capped at 8 named aux outputs with no stated cause. 3D renderers and multipass tools routinely emit 12 or more AOVs, and Strata's own target writes 12 aux layers.

A missing importer falls back to 'last cached proxy'. Export then either encodes proxy frames or fails, which contradicts both 'export never degrades' and durable outputs at full resolution for final-quality documents.

AEGP_EffectCallGeneric (PF_Cmd_COMPLETELY_GENERAL, an arbitrary data message to another instance) is mapped to fx.apply, which returns pixels only. Hosted binaries that exchange data between instances (Plexus objects and effectors, designer to instance) break.

The FFT kernels and audio.read are restricted to session events ('never in render'), yet Trapcode Form's live audio react is mapped to them, so Form-class audio reactivity would need baking instead of rendering live.

Every frame, the host polls the helper window frame with CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo or GetWindowRect for each docked Panelator panel. This hot UI path has no budget and no bench, and CGWindowList calls cost milliseconds.

fx.apply is specified three times with three different owners (ext-expr, effects-catalog, ext-runtime), while fx_host.rs actually implements it. The OP-COM owner, the expression host, is wrong, so behaviour does not live in one place.
Several records describe the same component: two SimCache records for one file, three interop-fence records and five aehost component records.

A.claim: Taint comes only from a plugin origin writing the expression. When the user applies a .ffx or resource.preset@1 that a plugin package ships or wrote, the result is tagged User, so plugin-shipped expression code runs in-process on expr-boa.

A plugin holding document.scripts and document.read:selection can write an expression on a selected property that reads out-of-scope layers, text or .json footage, then read the computed value back. This escalates its read scope.

Expression limits cover loops, recursion, depth and wall time but not memory. A tainted expression that allocates until V8 runs out of memory crashes ext-expr on every retry with no strike, while exports wait on that batch, so the export can stall forever.

Getters are served from the event's snapshot, while script-batching buffers writes and invalidates getters on write. A getter after a buffered setValue returns the stale pre-event value, which breaks AE scripts that read back what they wrote.

Rigwise runs imported .jsx rigs through extendscript@1 under its own origin, but its sheet is L1 without app.scripts, which plugin script runs require (L2). Either the permission is not enforced or the sheet is wrong.

Sound Keys updates its output levels live at render when a range box moves. Here output params are written only by jobs that bake keys (300 ms per 10,000 frames), so every range-box drag waits on a full rebake and cannot match the incumbent's speed.
The contract requires a monotone ease function, which excludes the overshoot, back, elastic and bounce eases that Flow and Ease and Wizz offer.

EffectCraft audio effects run at render and preview mixdown, 'not on a live audio thread', but the same API row also maps to the common class that runs EffectCraft audio slots on a dedicated real-time thread.

FFT is defined twice: once as a host spectrum kernel called by plugins (audio.spectrum), and once as a worker-side SIMD FFT over arena views with no app hop. This breaks the rule of one behaviour in one place.

T17 says callSystem 'runs only the declared pinned executable (no shell)'. The decision says callSystem with shell syntax runs the shell declaration (confinement full) when that grant is held. The test asserts the opposite and never covers the shell grant.

The ext-js component graph contradicts itself. CMP-EC-ext-js puts node-compat and cep-compat in craft-libs, while CMP-EC-ext-js-cep-compat says craft-extensions. node-compat depends on extendscript, though plain JS plugins and photoshop-compat use it. jsxbin and extendscript depend on each other.

There is one ext-expr worker per app process. That serialises expression evaluation across look-ahead, parallel frame renders and exports, while AE Multi-Frame Rendering evaluates rig expressions across cores. Export throughput for Duik-class rigs is unbudgeted and likely below AE.

No mapping between a Photoshop PSD filterFX entry for a third-party 8bf and the hosted command pshost.<sha256-prefix>.<name>. Existing Nik or Optics smart filters therefore open as 'not supported', and a binary update changes the command id.

8bf PICA ActionControl Play and 8LIZ execute run any app.batch command, but no record states which permissions the synthesised pshost principal holds or whether gate::admit checks each translated event.

The perms field lists only document.edit, but the op also writes the selection (selection.write), creates documents (new_document needs document.create) and, through Indexed convert:true, changes the document mode under what may be a selection-only scope.
Crashes are covered, but a hung 8bf that never calls abortProc/testAbort keeps the document busy forever. Nothing kills the helper or rolls back.

Wasm dab and tile brush engines run on the paint thread's schedule with 'strokes never dropped'. They have no deadline, watchdog or rollback, unlike the GPU path, so a looping engine stalls painting indefinitely.
Routing to a Job depends on a CostEma prediction. With no sample yet (first open, new mode or depth, new version), a 20 s filter runs inline and blocks the frame.

Wasm-only plugin adjustment layers, and non-separable Multichannel ones, run plugin code per tile inside compositor render. No budget is given and nothing says what happens when the plugin is slow or traps.

AI and neighbourhood incumbents (Topaz Photo AI, Nik Dfine, Portraiture, Retouch4me) trace only to a 100 MP point-filter cap. No budget exists for 100 MP apron or nn.run filters, so matching their speed is unproven.
WS10 has milestone M3 but depends on WS-COM-ws12 at M5, so the PhotoCraft adapter cannot finish before its native-host dependency.

Two component records own the same craft-pshost helper and the PhotoCraft pshost.rs mapping, with different layers (adapter and platform) and workstreams (WS12 and WS4). This breaks the one-place rule.

Each acquire cap says 'so the permission is document.create', but scanner and camera acquire modules also need devices.usb:picked. The six acquire caps and the filter-callbacks cap are 'tested' only by a GPU-device-availability test.
DEC-COM-v1-25 says 8bf hosting 'is built now', while DEC-PC-8bf-hosting-no-deferral says it supersedes v1 decision 25 as '8bf hosting excluded'. The two records disagree about what decision 25 was.

B.claim: WS10 is milestone M3 (CUT3 cuts at M3) but lists WS-COM-ws12 as a dependency, and WS12 is milestone M5. An M3 workstream cannot depend on one that delivers at M5.
Two component records own the same craft-pshost helper binary with different workstreams and layers, so its behaviour is not in one place.

The PICA support lists only ActionControl Play/Get and descriptors. The UIHooks suite (MainAppWindow, needed to parent dialogs) and the ColorSpace suite are not provided, and commercial 8bf filters that fail AcquireSuite for them will not run.

Acquire modules hold only document.create, but each band is written with pixels.write, and pixels.write requires document.edit. As written, the gate refuses every band, or document.edit is granted with no stated rule.
The detail says a write to the Selection target needs selection.write, but the op's perms list has only document.edit. Gate derivation from perms would not enforce selection.write.

brush.engine@1 says strokes are never dropped and final pixels are always the plugin's, but defines no deadline, trap or hang path for a Wasm (dabs/tiles) engine. A stuck engine leaves the stroke uncommitted and painting stalled.

The budgets let the Silver Efex-class flagship run 1.5x slower than native on CPU, and a hosted 8bf run 1.2x slower than native. Photoshop runs both in-process at native speed, so the incumbent is not matched.

The pshost helper is reaped after 60 s idle, so a later smart-filter re-render, Last Filter or Action step on an 8bf pays a process spawn, sandbox launch and module load with no budget. Photoshop keeps the module loaded in-process.
The 6x upscale has no time budget, only 'completes', so speed parity with Topaz Gigapixel 6x cannot be shown. The Lumina target covers only 2x.

RGB 8/16 adjustment layers bake to a fixed 33^3/65^3 LUT with no fallback. adjust.point@1 allows any colour-only function, and a discontinuous one (threshold, posterize) cannot meet the stated 1/1024 tolerance. RGB 32 and Multichannel do fall back to direct evaluation.

The capability makes full-resolution durable output the default only for documents of 16 bits or more, or over 24 MP, that are marked final, which implies proxy or ask otherwise. The decision says documents default to full. A proxy durable also blocks export when the plugin is missing.

The stroke buffer is always RGBA16F, which has an 11-bit mantissa and a 65504 maximum. Painting into 16-bit and 32-bit documents loses precision and range, against native-form interchange and Photoshop's own 16-bit painting.

A.claim: Setters update the mirror at once for read-your-writes, but the DomMirror contract is read-only and pushed by the worker only after commits. Derived values such as bounds after translate or the layer list after merge cannot be computed in the page, so unmodified UXP code reads stale data.

Symmetry modes, and the fan-out in CAP-PC-pen-symmetry-fanout, need one pen stroke to become N strokes. input.filter@1 transforms one stream into one 'user's stroke' and has no output for several strokes or for a single history step covering them.

The record says both compat layers run on the web build, with only process, open, .uxpaddon and devices failing. On the web, CEP *Sync calls, synchronousExecution and the sync endpoint cannot work, because browser main threads cannot block on a worker and service workers do not intercept sync XHR.

createSessionToken and getEntryForSessionToken are not mapped, and psdesc has no way to resolve a UXP token in a descriptor _path. Unmodified batchPlay calls such as open and placeEvent with _path: token fail unless the plugin holds files.paths.

Not mapped: executeAsModal timeOut, batchPlay modalBehavior (fail/wait/execute), historyStateInfo {name,target} and registerAutoCloseDocument. Because txn.modal queues other principals, a plugin that expects 'fail' or a timeout hangs instead of getting an error.

The decision fixes UXP panels as a separate OS window, which contradicts common docked modes in which photoshop-uxp@1 and CEP panels dock. REQ-PC-t6-limits caps T6 at 8 windows, a limit with no stated cause that an incumbent panel set can exceed.

On web, devices.ptp and devices.scan return -8 'because the browser cannot provide them'. That cause is wrong for PTP, because DEC-PC-devices-usb-webusb chose WebUSB semantics and Chromium browsers expose WebUSB, so tethering is restricted on web without a real cause.
tool.get/set is gated by app.session here, but the Shortcut Composer row says tool.set requires app.view. A permission that two records name differently cannot be enforced consistently.

BridgeTalk maps only the photoshop and aftereffects targets. Scripts that message illustrator, premierepro, indesign or bridge fire onError even though suite apps (VectorCraft, FilmCraft, DesignCraft, LightCraft) are installed beside PhotoCraft.

CSInterface.dispatchEvent, CSEvent scope (APPLICATION/GLOBAL) and Vulcan messages, which panels use to talk to each other, have no mapping. Only addEventListener and PhotoshopRegisterEvent are covered.

When a plugin picker owns app.intercept:color.picker, every fg, bg, swatch and style pick goes to it. No fallback is stated for a crashed, struck or hung picker, so a plugin can block all colour picking in the app until the 10-minute dialog idle cancel.

Plugin probe, format.thumbnail@1 for the start screen and Open Recent, and 8BIF FilterFile run on the Open and start-screen paths with no time budget. A slow or hung importer, especially as the Default opener, stalls Open and start-screen rendering.

app.run, app.batch and app.commands need PERM-COM-app.scripts (L2, 'run script engines, Actions, macros'), although every bridged command is already gated on its own Meta. Variables, components, styles and FigJam writes then need an extra L2 grant that Figma does not ask for.

Three records give three different rules for when a widget's state writes are exempt from collab.write: no document.edit; no permissions at all; or no permissions or only collab.read. A widget that holds only collab.presence or ui.open_url is exempt under one rule and refused under another.

In live sessions, automatic reactions run only on one elected runner. Yet document.changed caused by a peer grants no capabilities and writes from it return -2. When peer A drags, runner B cannot redraw the connectors, and A is not the runner, so Autoflow-class follow-ups never happen.

Past 1,024 entries the payload drops the ids and the plugin is told to re-read by revision through node.get. node.get has no revision parameter, no op lists the ids changed since a revision, and snapshot retention is unstated. Incremental lint has no defined path after truncation.

This hot event's budget is only a size cap (1,024 entries, one per frame). There is no latency budget from commit to delivery and no rule for delivery while the window is not painting. Flowline's 'track within one displayed frame' depends on that latency.

Shared namespaces must be declared in [share], but craft-ext import scans only for writes to derive collab.write and never derives [share] namespaces. Unmodified Figma plugins that call get/setSharedPluginData on any namespace are therefore refused.

Answering palette suggestions requires ui.window:floating (L1, OS windows), but the palette is drawn by the host and the context is a read-only Hook. Figma quick-action plugins need no permission for this, so the requirement has no cause.

The codegen result cache key (sha256, closure revision hash, preferences hash) does not include the language, unit or root_font_size, even though all three arrive in codegen.generate. Switching language or unit can show a stale cached block from another language.

The API row promises a 3 s codegen deadline (Figma parity). CON-FC-codegen@1 states 500 ms, CON-FC-hook-points says no number lives outside BUDGETS, and REQ-FC-remove-legacy removes the fixed budgets. The deadline a Figma codegen plugin actually gets is undefined.

The op says user.current is free 'except Render and Preview'. The identity contract says free 'except Render, Preview and Widget', so the records disagree about whether widget render can read the viewer.
The parity golden covers 'all six property-menu item types', but Figma's usePropertyMenu has seven, including link, which also involves the ui.open_url sheet. The link item is untested.

The same behaviour is specified more than once: test pairs that differ only in hyphens or underscores, three selection-not-broadcast tests, and OP-FC-* copies of OP-COM-* ops. The FC copies carry the hot flag and perms that the CAPs, which point via OP-COM, never see.

B.claim: The widget collab.write exemption has three different definitions. Under this one ("package holds no document.edit"), a widget holding files.read:any, clipboard.read or process.run can put what it reads into synced state and send it to the server without collab.write.

The server elects one runner per plugin for automatic reactions, but events caused by peers carry no capabilities and their writes return -2. The elected runner can never redraw after a peer's edit, so Autoflow/Flowline connectors go stale in live files.

app.run, app.batch and app.commands all require app.scripts. That adds a script-engine grant, with no stated cause, to every bridge call (Batch Styler, Chart, Blobs batches), and contradicts gating each call on its own Meta.

The perms of several op families mix up reads and writes. text.set, text.style.set, container.create/delete and doc.setActive list only document.read, so writes are not gated. prop.get, guide.list and relaunch.get demand document.edit for reads.

Past 1,024 entries the payload has no ids, and plugins are told to re-read "by revision" through node.get, which has no revision parameter. Deletes are lost and incremental plugins must rescan the whole document, while Figma delivers the full documentChanges list.

On live files cx.edit splits on max_changes into history.commit steps. That breaks the one undo step of batched edits and app.batch rollback, because the early steps are already broadcast. Figma keeps a large plugin edit as one undo step in multiplayer. max_changes has no value anywhere.

Flowline folds follow-up edits at frame rate into the user's drag undo step. But user and plugin edits must never share a collab batch, and one collab batch is one collab undo unit, so local undo and collab undo disagree. Batches at 60 Hz have no budget.

Only plugins declaring a namespace in [share] can read shared:<ns> data. Figma manifests have no such field and namespaces are runtime strings, so unmodified token and design-system plugins cannot exchange shared data. The read rule has no stated cause.

Answering quick-action suggestions requires ui.window:floating (OS windows and floating panels). That is a restriction with no cause on a palette step the host draws itself. Figma parameters need no permission, and palette windows are listed as free.

A stable user id shared by every app and plugin is free and undeclared, while the narrower per-plugin or per-vendor install_id needs a [licensing] declaration. The claim that the id leaves the machine only through live-document writes is also wrong: ui.open_url URLs and files.write can carry it.

Widget state (64 KiB default, up to 1 MiB, in widget:<id>) has no stated relation to the 16 MiB per-plugin and 64 MiB per-document quotas. A board with a few hundred poll widgets could hit -6 on a peer's click, and it is unclear whose account is charged.

"collab.write and collab.presence on by default behind switches" can be read as granted by default, which would leave the permissions unenforced. The capability also duplicates CAP-COM-live-collab-writes.

A.claim: Nine of the other apps (FilmCraft, VectorCraft, AniCraft and the rest) only 'follow after M6 in owner order'. They have no workstream, milestone, adapter task or acceptance test. The record's via is CMP-COM-ws2 (runtime core), not any adapter.

EC-T47b combines the VectorCraft live link with background render queue and farm submission. Relay acceptance runs EC-T47b only 'once VectorCraft has its adapter', which is never scheduled, so stream K and the Render Garden incumbent cannot close.
The EffectCraft bus.publish record duplicates the common one with no permission and a different broker. A suite-reach publish would then bypass the bus:<topic> check for topics of other vendors.

D-G allows native.full from any tier only for craft-aehost, the OFX bridge and video-output helpers. The Kiln Community build still ships the native.full kiln-live helper and cites D-G, so it is either refused or granted outside the decision.

The per-PR thresholds disagree: FigCraft fails a PR at a 5% regression and gates owner-task CPU ns, while common C17 fails at 2% instructions or any logical counter increase and only reports thread CPU ns.

Records disagree on which owner decisions are open. One lists D-K and D-T, two list D-D, D-K and D-T, and two app-level decisions (FigCraft and PhotoCraft) are also open-owner although app docs may keep no decisions of their own.

D-T is restated in five records with different blocked sets. A decided record and the proof criteria assume D-T hardware, while the built state only reports wall-clock. Real-time audio and GPU hot-path budgets go unenforced, and M6 cannot close with D-T open.

Prism ships at M4 and needs the PhotoCraft and FigCraft web builds. The FigCraft web build is in F10, bundled with T6 on CEF, which common schedules at M5. App workstreams use FC-order, pc-stream or 'after P1b' instead of M-milestones, so M4 readiness cannot be checked.
The flagship workstream depends on M6, but M6's exit is 'all flagships green' and lists no dependencies, which is a cycle. M6 is also dated week 66, while the replan puts M6 at weeks 74-82.

Each CUT gate is a required job 'on the three runners'. On hosted runners this exceeds the cap of two macOS jobs per PR, since unit and sandbox already use both. On D-T runners, CUT1 at M2 is blocked by an open decision.

Plugin printer presets are limited to local printers with no stated cause. The OS spooler reaches network printers, not the plugin, so DEC-COM-no-plugin-network does not apply. Photoshop print plug-ins can use any OS printer.

The pshost native-UI profile says 'no lpacCom', but the PhotoCraft decision and craft-aehost put lpacCom behind lpac_com_native_ui and C-LPAC. The two hosts' profiles diverge, and 8bf dialogs that need COM fail on Windows.

Before-save/export hook timeout is 2 s default here and in QAS-SEC-plugin-never-stalls-ui, but the BUDGETS row gives BeforeHook 500 ms per hook point shared by all plugins. Save latency differs by 4x depending on which record is built.

Plugins passing endpoint or server params get two different codes. Exposure@2 and the FC N6 list say Endpoint params are -9 Excluded, distinct from -2. The PhotoCraft print sink returns -2 'param not plugin-settable' for server/endpoint/devMode.

FC's gesture-only set differs from the single context table. FC makes all of history.control and document.lifecycle:* gesture-only. Common runs history.control:snapshot and lifecycle save/versions in Automatic with app.automation: an uncaused restriction and a second context.rs.

'files.*' is a permission row at L2, but its family contains files.write:home, files.paths and files.write:any at L4. Under 'broader covers narrower within a family', an L2 consent covers L4 file writes, and the row also breaks 'closed enum, no wildcard'.

Two incompatible process.run vocabularies. COM has process.run:<decl> plus a confinement key and process.run:<id>, all L3. SEC has process.run, process.run:confined (L3), process.run:full (L4) and process.run:shell (L4, shell only in SEC). The parser and sheet cannot follow both.

Nine D-D records disagree on what is built. COM says docked panels are built and tested behind CefDockedCompat/CefDocked switches. FC and SEC say only CefWindow is built and 'docked web panels need owner decision', which defers building docked mode in FC.

FC runs L1-L3 jobs on a separate headless job device but shows results on the eframe device without readback. That is a cross-device copy, which contradicts probation and plugin GPU work on the app device under one MemAccount. The 4K RGBA16F within 15 ms budget then cannot hold.

Probation isolation rules conflict. Common says probation is on the app device with isolation only on Metal. EC says an isolated device is used when the user enables it in the manager or S-G1 proves isolation. GPU probation and invariants also live in EffectCraft components, not ext-gpu.

Platform crates are defined twice with different layers, workstreams and deps. ext-js is platform (COM ws4/ws12) and sdk (EC stream-n); ext-expr is in COM ws9 and EC stream-g. Similar copies exist for jsxbin, node-compat, ext-runtime-output and a triple gate (COM, EC, SEC) despite one gate.
